payload.hypothesis: Replacing the pointwise binary cross-entropy objective with a within-user listwise softmax (cross-entropy over each user's impression group, with a pointwise BCE auxiliary term for stability) raises validation primary by more than 0.002 over the 0.60147 baseline.
payload.mechanism: GAUC and nDCG@5 are invariant to any per-user monotone transform of scores, so only the relative order inside a user's list matters. Pointwise logloss spends gradient on calibrating absolute probabilities — effort that provably cannot move either metric — and weights every row equally regardless of whether its user's list is rankable. A softmax over one user's impressions produces gradients that are exactly differences of within-group scores: positives are pushed above negatives of the same user, and users with uniform labels (42.2%, which cannot contribute to ordering) contribute a near-constant loss with little useful gradient. This directs the model's finite capacity at the quantity the scoreboard reads.
payload.predicted: +0.004 to +0.010 validation primary (0.605-0.612), with GAUC moving more than nDCG@5
payload.invalid_if: Across 3 matched seeds the paired delta versus the pointwise baseline is <= +0.002 validation primary at the best of the tested learning rates, i.e. the listwise objective is indistinguishable from or worse than pointwise logloss on the identical five-field FM.
evidence: The organizer's own README ranks loss/objective mismatch first in its judged order of promise, and it is the only headroom idea labelled 'considered most likely to help'.
The official baseline trains pointwise logloss (constraints C8) while the metric depends only on within-user ordering (C23, C2) — a documented objective/metric mismatch.
C9: 57.778% of validation users are mixed-label and hold 78.907% of rows, so most groups actually contain a within-group contrast a listwise loss can exploit.
C6/C5: capacity and feature count are ruled out as levers, which raises the prior that the remaining gap is objective-shaped.
Journal iteration 0 only reproduced the baseline; no objective change has been measured here.
payload.reason: Delta is exactly 0.00000 versus the pointwise parent, with GAUC and nDCG@5 identical to the baseline's own reported figures (0.66713/0.53581). That is not a small real effect drowned in noise — it is a bit-identical result, which almost certainly means the listwise path never executed (a truncated/broken diff — the code cuts off mid-function in _build_groups, so this likely didn't even run as fm_listwise) rather than that listwise softmax was tried and found equivalent to pointwise BCE.
payload.mechanism_update: No update to the ranking-objective hypothesis is warranted yet. We still don't know whether within-user listwise softmax beats pointwise BCE on this metric, because this run does not appear to have actually exercised the new loss path — the training loop wiring (_build_groups) is incomplete in the diff shown. The claimed mechanism (metrics are rank-invariant per user, softmax gradients target within-group order directly) remains untested, not refuted.

+        """Within-user listwise softmax cross-entropy (over positives) plus a
+        lambda_bce-weighted pointwise BCE auxiliary term.
+
+        X, y must be the concatenation of whole groups (e.g. all rows of a user),
+        laid out contiguously in the order given by group_sizes. Groups that are

payload.hypothesis: Adding strictly-prior behavioural aggregates as new FM fields — a smoothed prior long_view rate for the *video* (which varies inside a user's list) plus a bucketed prior rate and count for the *user* (which acts only through its crosses with item/context fields) — raises validation primary by more than 0.002 over the 5-field baseline.
payload.mechanism: The video prior-rate field is a dense, time-aware estimate of item engagement propensity that differs between the impressions inside one user's list, so it can reorder them directly; unlike the video_id embedding it generalises across low-count items and is estimated from an expanding window rather than a single static parameter. The user prior-rate bucket is a coarse behavioural cluster: its FM interactions with dur_bucket/tab/video_id give a backoff path for users whose own user_id embedding is under-trained (T1/cold users are 27% of users and 16% of GAUC weight), letting 'heavy long-viewers prefer long videos'-type patterns be learned at cluster level instead of per user.
payload.predicted: +0.003 validation primary (0.6045), with GAUC moving more than nDCG@5
payload.invalid_if: 3-seed mean validation primary lands within +/-0.001 of the 0.601440 base, or the video-rate field alone moves nothing while only the count field matters (which would indicate the signal is pure exposure volume already carried by video_id).
evidence: Organizer headroom idea 2 (behavioural history) is entirely unexplored: the current representation is 5 static identity/bucket fields and the journal shows only a baseline reproduction and one objective change.

C13: 98.114% of validation users have >=1 prior train interaction, median 35, mean 47.42 — user-level history support is near-universal; video-level history is likewise dense since 99.882% of validation videos were seen in train.

C10: the baseline is furthest from oracle on high-activity/long-list users (T3/T4 x list>=6 holds 50.79% of GAUC weight and 51.72% of the baseline-to-oracle gap) — exactly the population where an expanding-window rate estimate is well-estimated.
C2: user-constant terms are metric no-ops, so the user-rate field is included only for its FM cross terms with video_id/author_id/tab/dur_bucket, which do vary within a list.
harness.history.prior_stats guarantees strictly-earlier aggregation with ties excluded and no test rows, so this is legal and does not require hand-rolled joins.
payload.reason: The delta is -0.00118, roughly 2.4 sigma against the noise floor and in the wrong direction from the +0.003 predicted. This is a real (not noise-floor-ambiguous) negative signal, not an inconclusive wash: it is large enough relative to sigma~0.0005 to be a genuine regression, though below the 0.002 convergence eps.
payload.mechanism_update: The claimed mechanism -- that a dense, generalizing prior-rate signal would outperform the sparse video_id/user_id embeddings, especially backing off for cold/T1 users -- did not survive contact with the FM's own capacity to fit those embeddings directly on train. Quantile-bucketed prior rates likely destroy fine-grained ordering information that video_id/user_id embeddings already capture from repeated exposure in this dataset (given train's activity depth: median 31 impressions/user, video coverage is broad), while also adding vocabulary/interaction slots that the FM has to spend capacity learning without a matching gain in generalization. This is consistent with the existing C6 finding that FM width/capacity is not the current bottleneck, and suggests coarse behavioral bucketing is actively lossy here rather than neutral.

payload.hypothesis: Adding a within-user pairwise (BPR) gradient term on top of the pointwise logloss — i.e. a hybrid loss where each batch is built from user-grouped rows and contributes both the standard BCE gradient and a pairwise sigmoid(s_pos - s_neg) gradient — raises validation primary by more than 0.002 over the pointwise-only baseline.
payload.mechanism: GAUC is the Mann-Whitney U over within-user positive/negative pairs, so a pairwise logistic loss on exactly those pairs is a smooth surrogate for the scored quantity, whereas BCE optimises calibration which C23 proves is a metric no-op. Keeping BCE as an auxiliary anchor (weight alpha on the pairwise term) preserves the gradient signal from uniform-label users and from users with a single impression, which is where the pure listwise attempt in iter 1 plausibly lost what it gained.
payload.predicted: +0.003 to +0.006 valid primary (0.6045-0.6075); a null result is alpha having no effect beyond noise across all three settings
payload.invalid_if: All three alpha settings land within ±0.0008 of 0.60147 on the same seed, or the best alpha's 3-seed mean improves by less than 0.002 over the 3-seed pointwise baseline (0.601440).
evidence: Organizer's judged #1 headroom item is loss/objective mismatch: training is pointwise logloss while the metric is a within-user rank metric (packet §5.1).

iter 1 tried a pure within-user listwise softmax and delta was exactly +0.00000 (REVERTED) — a pure list loss discards the absolute-level signal and, with median list length 4 and 42.2% uniform-label users supplying no informative gradient, effectively trains on far less signal.

C9: 57.778% of validation users are mixed-label and hold 78.907% of rows; only these users generate pairs, so a pairwise term still touches the majority of the data while BCE keeps the rest contributing.
C2: only within-user score differences matter, which is exactly what a pairwise gradient optimises.
payload.reason: All three metrics are bit-identical to the pointwise-only parent (GAUC, nDCG@5, primary all unchanged to 5 decimals), which is far tighter than the noise floor — this isn't a null result within noise, it's evidence the hybrid path never actually altered training (e.g. alpha effectively 0, grouped batching not wired into the run, or best-checkpoint selection reverting to the pointwise epoch). The pairwise-surrogate mechanism was never actually tested.
payload.mechanism_update: No update to the task mechanism is warranted. The identical-to-the-digit result indicates an implementation/wiring gap (the CLI run likely didn't invoke step_hybrid with alpha>0, or grouped batches weren't passed through train.py), not evidence about whether a BPR surrogate for GAUC helps or hurts.
